If narration changes, use Apenas entró Ramiro, señaló, the gloss Apenas entró Ramiro = As soon as Ramiro came in, and in ch208 Apenas puso el último tornillo, alguien se sentó.

The line is correct Spanish and nothing I could reach confines conditional como to Spain: the RAE grammar text seen in a search summary gives no regional mark and a Mexican dictionary is reported as recording the use, while the claim's NGLE citation stays unverified (rae.es refused access and the web search budget ran out). This is the same open question as LC1-016, and p:como-me-entere, the u54 and u57 rows, ch179 and this line's gloss entry stand or fall together, so a Colombian speaker decides first; Si no respira, mija, se me desmaya is sound if the answer is no.

reason: A consistency fix rather than an error, since cola is understood everywhere: l:fila names cola as its Peninsular pair, and El Tiempo's Bogotá reporting says largas filas and haciendo fila. Hernando la midió still agrees, gate --fix must recompute the chapter's lexemes, and no check needs l:cola in this chapter, though it is a u45 d4 lexeme and its queue rows (u45-0351, u45-0742, u45-0743, u45-0745) want the same review; ch180's print queue stays.

The 2010 Ortografía treats rio as a spelling monosyllable and dropped the 1999 option of the accent (Fundéu wording and the DPD tilde entry via search summaries; rae.es refused access), check/exact.ts already calls rió the legacy spelling, and the tagger reads se rio as l:reír in 54 chapters. This is the same edit as LA2-067 in batch-04, so whichever applies first finishes it; the claim's guión point is a separate sweep of ch151, ch152, the u47 rows and the id l:guión.
